metadata.updatePolicy: Every shipped user-facing feature, support-content change, or bug fix gets an entry here. Test-only, CI-only, and internal refactors are not listed.

updates.title: Call Documentation moved to a global docked live tool
updates.changed: Moved Call Documentation out of Training & Resources and into the authenticated sidebar as a global live tool. Opening Call Documentation no longer navigates away from the agent’s current page. The compact right-side dock stays available while the agent browses Navigator, Common Issues, process guides, Device Walkthroughs, Scripts & Communication, Updates, Feedback, or admin pages. Agents can minimize the dock to a small bar or close it without losing the current local draft; only Clear removes the call information.
checks: From Navigator, select Call Documentation in the sidebar and confirm the current page does not change while the right-side dock opens.
Enter a caller name and exact issue, navigate to another page, and confirm the same documentation draft remains visible.
Select Minimize and confirm the dock collapses to a small bar; restore it and confirm the entered draft is still present.
Close Call Documentation, reopen it from the sidebar, and confirm the draft is still present until Clear is used.
Open Training & Resources and confirm Documentation is no longer a training tab; Device Walkthroughs, Scripts & Communication, and Video Library remain available.

updates.title: Phase 5 call documentation workspace added
updates.changed: Introduced the Phase 5 call documentation fields and copy-ready summary. The workspace is now accessed globally from the sidebar as a docked live tool rather than as a Training & Resources tab; see the newer global documentation dock update for the current workflow.
checks: Use the newer Call Documentation sidebar tool for the current workflow.
Confirm the same approved fields and copy-ready summary remain available in the global dock.
Confirm caller-entered text remains local to the active browser session and is not included in OGCon analytics or feedback context.

updates.title: Scenario discovery now guides the next approved step
updates.changed: Replaced the static Discovery Questions block in Scenario Scripts with interactive answer choices. Agents can select what the caller reports and OGCon immediately narrows the next approved action or suggests the correct linked route. All 19 Scenario Scripts now have guided discovery, including device-, role-, state-, and permission-specific branching where it changes the support path.
checks: Open Training & Resources → Scripts & Communication → Scenario Scripts → Bluetooth Headset.
Select Connected to this device → They can’t hear me → Windows and confirm the recommendation changes to Select the headset as Zoom Microphone.
Switch to Can’t Join, choose Waiting Room, and confirm OGCon recommends the Waiting to Get In route instead of continuing failed-join troubleshooting.
Switch between scenarios and confirm discovery answers reset rather than leaking into the next caller scenario.

updates.title: Scenario Scripts expanded from 9 to 19 live-call scenarios
updates.changed: Added ten specialized scripts to the existing Phase 4 live-call structure: Bluetooth Headset, Secure Connection Error, Transfer to Another Device, Join Muted, Camera On / Off on Join, Meeting Volume, Auto Computer Audio, Specific Audio Input Channels, Who Is Already in the Meeting?, and Invite / Copy Link. Each script remains linked to its approved Common Issue route and source processes.
checks: Open Scenario Scripts and confirm all 19 scenario tabs are available.
Open Secure Connection Error and confirm the script clearly limits that specialty path to the documented Mac error.
Open Join Muted and confirm connected-but-muted is kept separate from Don’t connect to audio.
Open Invite / Copy Link and confirm the script explains the technical control without deciding who is authorized to attend.

updates.title: Report an issue is global and captures the current screen context
updates.changed: Moved Report an issue to the global console shell so it stays visible across pages and resized windows. Reports now capture the current page, selected tab, section, active device, caller role, Common Issue, process/category IDs, browser path, viewport size, browser user agent, and client timestamp. Admin Feedback Queue can display the captured context for troubleshooting.
checks: Resize the browser narrowly and confirm Report an issue remains visible at the lower-right corner.
Submit a report from a Common Issue or Training scenario and confirm the active tab/section is captured.
In Admin → Feedback Queue, expand Captured screen context and confirm route, viewport, browser, and available live-call context are shown.

updates.title: What’s New now follows a clear release-entry rule
updates.changed: Defined the What’s New page as the user-facing release log for OGCon. Every shipped user-facing feature, support-content change, or bug fix must receive an update entry. Test-only changes, CI maintenance, and invisible internal refactors stay out of the user-facing log so the page remains useful instead of becoming raw commit history.
checks: Open What’s New / Updates and confirm September 19 entries appear above the September 18 history.
Confirm the Update policy note explains which shipped changes are listed.
Confirm the header/version chip now shows the latest update date from the newest change-log entry.

updates.title: Common Issue Routes added to Navigator
updates.changed: Added the first Phase 2 live-call routing layer for five high-frequency concerns: Can’t join the meeting, I can’t hear anyone, They can’t hear me, My camera isn’t working, and I’m waiting to get in. Each route starts from the caller’s symptom, asks only the questions that change the path, separates symptoms from assumed causes, shows one-step-at-a-time guidance and expected results, keeps Waiting for host distinct from Waiting Room, carries forward the Phase 1 device/role/status context, and preserves access to approved Process Documents plus traceable official Zoom Support sources. Natural caller-language search now surfaces these fast routes before deeper process results when appropriate.
checks: Search I cant hear you and confirm the Audio-output Common Issue Route appears first instead of a connection diagnosis.
Open I’m waiting to get in and confirm Waiting for host and Waiting Room are explained as separate meeting states with different next actions.
Choose a Phase 1 device and caller role, open a Common Issue Route, and confirm the selected context appears inside the route.
Open Full Process from a route and confirm the original approved Process Documents remain available without modified source wording.
Open Sources and confirm official Zoom Support references and the verification date are visible; any known internal/current-source discrepancy should be flagged rather than silently reconciled.

updates.title: Core Live Call Flow added to Navigator
updates.changed: Added the Phase 1 live-call foundation at the top of Navigator: Opening → Acknowledgment → Identify → Resolution → Recap → Adjacent Issues → Closing. The flow uses Step / Agent Action / Suggested Script columns, includes device selection for Windows, Mac, iPhone, Android, and Browser, identifies Host vs Participant, and records Resolved / Unresolved / Escalation Needed status. The previous four-step workflow banner was removed so agents see one clear call journey. Existing search and process tools remain available below the flow.
checks: Open Navigator and confirm Live Call Flow is the first primary work block before Search and the process library.
Select a device, Host or Participant, and a resolution status; each selected option should remain visibly pressed.
Use Reset call and confirm all call-context selections clear for the next caller.
Resize to mobile width and confirm each call-flow row remains readable as Step, Agent Action, and Suggested Script without horizontal clipping.

updates.title: Strict QA findings remediated
updates.changed: Resolved the strict QA findings that affected live-call usability and accessibility. Closed mobile navigation is no longer keyboard-focusable, natural caller-language search now routes key support phrases more reliably, long Call Guides use progressive disclosure without removing approved content, avatar selection and process tabs have efficient keyboard behavior, form errors identify their fields, dialogs prevent background scrolling, and the active navigation item is announced to assistive technology. Supabase hardening also removed unintended client execution of an internal SECURITY DEFINER helper, moved citext out of the exposed public schema, optimized RLS auth checks, and added missing foreign-key indexes.
checks: On tablet/mobile widths, keep the sidebar closed and confirm keyboard focus stays on visible controls; open it and confirm navigation becomes available.
Search mic not working, They can’t hear me, stuck waiting room, host hasnt started meeting, and Where is the share screen button? and confirm the intended support route ranks first.
Open a long Call Guide and confirm only the first set of steps, scripts, and very long callouts are shown initially, with Show remaining controls preserving access to all approved content.
Use keyboard-only navigation in the avatar picker and process tabs, and confirm validation errors identify the relevant form field.
Open a process/profile/training/report dialog and confirm the page behind it does not scroll.

updates.title: Final QA gate and landmark accessibility cleanup
updates.changed: Completed the pre-revamp release QA gate. Removed the nested main landmark from the Navigator, expanded the permanent Smart Search acceptance matrix, and added regression checks for visible keyboard focus, narrow and zoomed layouts, reduced motion, responsive navigation, and search-suggestion clipping.
checks: Use keyboard-only navigation and confirm interactive controls show a visible focus ring.

Resize the browser through compact desktop, tablet, and narrow mobile widths and confirm navigation, cards, process drawers, feedback actions, and admin usage controls remain reachable without horizontal clipping.
Enable reduced motion in the operating system and confirm transitions/animations are minimized.
Search CAN'T HEAR, microphone issue, camra not working, cant jion, bluetooh, screen share, and share screen and confirm the intended approved processes remain discoverable.

updates.title: Privacy-safe usage, presence, and feedback administration
updates.changed: Connected the existing analytics tables to the Support Console. Authenticated sessions now heartbeat roughly once per minute, active time stops after five minutes without interaction, stale presence is treated as offline, Usage Analytics includes zero-usage users with Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Custom views, and the Feedback Queue now supports audited status changes plus Open Page routing. Production CI also moved to Node 24 for compatibility with the current Supabase packages.
checks: Sign in, use the Navigator, and confirm Admin Usage Analytics begins showing privacy-safe activity without storing search text, notes, clipboard content, or customer form values.
Leave the Console untouched for more than five minutes and confirm the account becomes Idle rather than continuing to accumulate active time; stale heartbeat records should display Offline.
In Usage Analytics, switch between Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Custom and confirm every team member remains listed even when they have zero events.
In Feedback Queue, change a report status and confirm its history is recorded, then use Open Page to return to the stored process or safe Console page.

updates.title: Dialogs, copy actions, training links, and admin actions stabilized
updates.changed: Repaired Feedback Cancel navigation, exact Related Training deep-links, per-button copy success/failure states, dialog Escape/focus trapping/focus restoration, profile save error recovery, and duplicate-submit protection for admin actions.
checks: Cancel from the Feedback page and confirm you remain inside the Support Console.
Open a Related Training item from a process and confirm the exact selected video opens.
Use multiple Copy controls and confirm only the clicked control shows Copied ✓ or Copy failed.
Open process, report, profile, and admin dialogs with the keyboard and confirm Escape closes them and focus returns to the opener.

updates.title: Sidebar footer stays visible in wide but short windows
updates.changed: Extended the sidebar vertical-space protection to every browser width. When the window is wide but vertically short, the navigation list now owns the scrolling space while the console metadata and Logout remain anchored and readable instead of being pushed below the viewport.

Confirm the navigation list scrolls when needed while Console v1.0, Owner Cjei A., Collaborator Nina F., and Logout remain visible.
Repeat with the admin account, where the navigation list is longest, and confirm the footer remains readable.

updates.title: Mobile admin drawer keeps console metadata visible
updates.changed: Adjusted the short-window mobile and tablet drawer so the navigation list scrolls inside its own area instead of pushing the console metadata off-screen. Console version, update and review dates, Owner Cjei A., Collaborator Nina F., and Logout remain readable at the bottom, and the drawer width adapts to the available screen width.
checks: Open the hamburger menu while the browser is narrow and vertically short, especially while signed in as an admin.
Confirm the navigation list can scroll without pushing the console metadata below the screen.
Confirm Console v1.0, Owner Cjei A., Collaborator Nina F., and Logout remain fully visible and readable at the bottom of the open drawer.

updates.title: Workspace now follows browser window resizing progressively
updates.changed: Improved responsive behavior so the support workspace reflows in stages as the browser window becomes narrower instead of waiting for one mobile breakpoint. The Navigator main columns stack on compact desktop, category cards and workflow steps reduce from multiple columns as space tightens, and the mobile sidebar still switches to the off-canvas drawer at tablet widths.
checks: Start with the browser maximized, then slowly drag the window narrower and confirm content reflows without horizontal clipping or overlapping.
Around compact desktop widths, confirm Common Issues moves below the main category section before the cards become cramped.
Continue narrowing the window and confirm category cards move from three columns to two, then one, while the four-step workflow becomes two columns, then one.
At tablet/mobile widths, confirm the fixed sidebar changes to the hamburger drawer and leaves no hidden strip or content overlap.

updates.title: What’s New / Updates and console metadata
updates.changed: Added a shared update history for user-facing changes, plus visible console version, effective date, last updated date, owner, collaborator, and next review information.

updates.title: Duplicate combined Suggested Script removed
updates.changed: Removed the long combined Suggested Script block that repeated scripts already shown under individual steps. Per-step scripts remain where they are needed, while source-level scripts are shown once as Additional Source Script.

updates.title: Smart Search and live suggestions
updates.changed: Search now normalizes case, apostrophes, punctuation, and spacing; understands controlled support aliases and synonyms; tolerates close typos; shows suggestions from short prefixes; keeps the list to six results; keeps the dropdown fully visible; and opens the exact process selected.

updates.title: Responsive sidebar and compact header stabilized
updates.changed: Unified the authenticated console at the 800px breakpoint, fixed tablet overlap and hidden-sidebar slivers, added click-outside closing, closed the drawer after navigation, exposed menu state for accessibility, and corrected the compact Zoom Support Console brand alignment.

updates.title: Accessible category icons and keyboard search controls
updates.changed: Added distinct visual icons to support category cards and retained keyboard-friendly search suggestion controls so agents can move through suggestions with the keyboard.
